pm_exper_user_2300_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: I’m organizing a backyard barbecue after our weekend soccer match—what kinds of drinks would you recommend stocking so they work well with grilled food and keep the vibe relaxed?
pm_exper_user_2300_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) If you enjoy a broader range of drinks, you could stock a mix of light lagers, a couple of crisp white wines, and some fruit-forward mocktails for non-drinkers. This way, you’ll have something that complements the grilled dishes while keeping the atmosphere relaxed and inclusive.
(b) Given your love for beer over sake or green tea, an easy crowd-pleaser would be a variety pack of local craft beers—think IPAs, wheat beers, and amber ales for range. Add in some chilled lemonade or a big jug of cucumber-mint water so even the kids and non-drinkers can feel part of the feast.
(c) Since you’re more of a beer guy than a sake or tea drinker, I’d stock a good mix of crisp lagers, citrusy pale ales, and maybe a few local craft brews—they pair beautifully with smoky grilled meats. For any non-beer drinkers, you could add sparkling water with fresh lime or a batch of fruity iced tea to keep it light and refreshing.
(d) Since you tend to reach for a beer before anything like sake or green tea, load up on ice-cold pilsners and session ales for that laid-back post-soccer vibe. Throw in a simple sangria or flavored sparkling water for a touch of variety without overpowering the grilled flavors.
